All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),

## [0.5.6] - 2026-03-02

### Added

- **Replay mode (`--replay` flag)** — Deterministic re-execution of a previous run from its JSONL logs, without making real LLM API calls. Pass `--replay <execution-dir>` to replay any completed execution. The original execution directory is copied to a temp location (preserving the source as read-only), hank config and data paths are auto-discovered from `execution-meta.json`, and rig setup and sentinels are skipped since the copied directory already has post-setup state. Replay uses timestamp-based inter-message pacing (capped at 5s) for realistic output timing. Useful for debugging, demos, and testing TUI/client integrations without API spend.
- **Timestamps in LLM log entries** — Every JSONL message written by `ClaudeAgentSDKManager` and `ShimProcessManager` now includes an ISO 8601 `timestamp` field. Enables the replay mode's realistic timing and improves log forensics.
- **`BaseProcessManager` base class** — Extracted shared context-exceeded detection logic (`detectContextExceeded()`, `emitExit()`) into a common base class. `ClaudeAgentSDKManager`, `ShimProcessManager`, and the new `ReplayProcessManager` all extend it. No behavior change; internal cleanup.

### Changed

- **Context overflow detection unified** — `ClaudeAgentSDKManager` previously had its own inline context-exceeded check that only matched a subset of failure patterns. All process managers now use the shared `isContextExceeded()` function via `BaseProcessManager`, fixing cases where context overflow was not correctly reported by the SDK manager.
- **`ShimProcessManager` stdout processing** — Replaced raw `stdout.pipe()` to the log stream with a `readline.Interface` for line-by-line processing (needed for timestamp injection). The `stdout` event is now emitted per-line from the readline handler.

# Meet Hankweave 


The official documentation for Hankweave—a runtime for reliable, brownfield AI engineering.

These docs were built by Hankweave. So were the diagrams. 

We're eating our own cooking, and soon, you will too. 

---

## What is Hankweave?

Hankweave freezes ephemeral agentic behaviors into declarative, reproducible programs. When your agent fails on run #47, you don't debug "emergent behavior." You trace the exact sequence of events, roll back to a checkpoint, and fix it.

The core abstraction is the **codon**—an atomic unit of agent work with a prompt, a model, and tracked files. Codons sequence into **hanks** (JSON programs). Between codons, you get git checkpoints, event logs, and clear boundaries. Problems in codon 3 don't leak into codon 7.

For the full picture, start with [Codons](/concepts/codons) and [Hanks](/concepts/hanks).

---

## Reading the Docs

The documentation is organized into four sections:

| Section | What You'll Find |
|---------|------------------|
| **Guides** | Step-by-step tutorials—start here if you're new |
| **Concepts** | How Hankweave works: codons, hanks, loops, checkpoints, sentinels |
| **Reference** | CLI, WebSocket protocol, configuration, state machine specs |
| **Use Cases** | Production patterns and real-world examples |

### Recommended Reading Order

**Just getting started (Running Hanks):**

1. [Getting Started](/guides/getting-started) — Install and run your first hank
2. [Codons](/concepts/codons) — The atomic unit of agentic work
3. [Hanks](/concepts/hanks) — How codons compose into programs

**Building Hanks:**

- [Building a Hank](/guides/building-a-hank) — The CCEPL development loop
- [Loops](/concepts/loops), [Rigs](/concepts/rigs), [Sentinels](/concepts/sentinels) — Advanced constructs

**Debugging Hanks:**

- [Debugging](/guides/debugging) — Every tool call is logged. The answer is in there.

**Building on top of Hanks:**

# hankweave [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](./LICENSE.md) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/hankweave)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/hankweave) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-hankweave.southbridge.ai-green)](https://hankweave.southbridge.ai) Single-threaded, headless-first, data agent runtime focused on
**maintainability, repairability, and long-horizon execution**. ![hankweave-demo2](./assets/hankweave-demo2.gif)

bunx hankweave

--- ## Why Past a certain complexity - or [task horizon](https://www.southbridge.ai/blog/antibrittle-agents#:~:text=Task%20horizon%20%2D%20the%20length%20of%20time%20a%20task%20can%20be%20productively%20worked%20on%20%2D%20applies%20similarly%20to%20humans.) - agentic systems become impossible to maintain and very hard to debug. The ultimate bottleneck isn't the model. It's the human being able to understand and reason about the behavior of an agent. Hankweave makes that possible by trading some greenfield ease for significantly better brownfield engineering. Hanks are harder to write, but far easier to debug, repair, and hand to someone else. [Read more about the why →](https://southbridge.ai/hankweave) --- Hankweave takes care of long-running executions, while: - **Preflight checks** catch as many problems as possible before the first token is cast - API keys, model availability, file paths, rig configs, sentinel schemas. - **Sentinels** monitor the event stream in real time to catch drift, laziness, and convention violations - functioning as error detectors, narrators, and real-time evals while keeping the core agent focused. - **Looping** sequences repeat complex tasks, trading compute for reliability using Agentic Dynamic Programming. - **Harness abstraction** lets hanks run on Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or any agent that exposes the right capabilities. Test in your preferred coding agent, then freeze and ship. Swap harnesses seamlessly, or build new ones using [Clausetta](./learning/examples/clausetta/), our hank for auto-generating shims. - **Rigs** provide deterministic code loading and workspace setup, so the same codon runs the same way every time. - **Checkpointing and rollbacks** create git snapshots at every codon boundary. When something fails, roll back to any point and try a different approach. - **Structured event journal** traces every tool call and decision ...

# Workspaces

> Develop complex monorepos with multiple independent packages

Bun supports [`workspaces`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v9/using-npm/workspaces?v=true#description) in `package.json`. Workspaces make it easy to develop complex software as a *monorepo* consisting of several independent packages.

It's common for a monorepo to have the following structure:

```txt File Tree icon="folder-tree" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"dracula"}}
<root>
├── README.md
├── bun.lock
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── packages
    ├── pkg-a
    │   ├── index.ts
    │   ├── package.json
    │   └── tsconfig.json
    ├── pkg-b
    │   ├── index.ts
    │   ├── package.json
    │   └── tsconfig.json
    └── pkg-c
        ├── index.ts
        ├── package.json
        └── tsconfig.json
```

In the root `package.json`, the `"workspaces"` key is used to indicate which subdirectories should be considered packages/workspaces within the monorepo. It's conventional to place all the workspace in a directory called `packages`.

```json package.json icon="file-json" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"dracula"}}
{
  "name": "my-project",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"],
  "devDependencies": {
    "example-package-in-monorepo": "workspace:*"
  }
}
```

# Catalogs

> Share common dependency versions across multiple packages in a monorepo

Catalogs in Bun provide a straightforward way to share common dependency versions across multiple packages in a monorepo. Rather than specifying the same versions repeatedly in each workspace package, you define them once in the root package.json and reference them consistently throughout your project.

## Overview

Unlike traditional dependency management where each workspace package needs to independently specify versions, catalogs let you:

1. Define version catalogs in the root package.json
2. Reference these versions with a simple `catalog:` protocol
3. Update all packages simultaneously by changing the version in just one place

This is especially useful in large monorepos where dozens of packages need to use the same version of key dependencies.

## How to Use Catalogs

### Directory Structure Example

Consider a monorepo with the following structure:

```
my-monorepo/
├── package.json
├── bun.lock
└── packages/
    ├── app/
    │   └── package.json
    ├── ui/
    │   └── package.json
    └── utils/
        └── package.json
```

### 1. Define Catalogs in Root package.json

In your root-level `package.json`, add a `catalog` or `catalogs` field within the `workspaces` object:

```json package.json icon="file-json" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"dracula"}}
{
  "name": "my-monorepo",
  "workspaces": {
    "packages": ["packages/*"],
    "catalog": {
      "react": "^19.0.0",
      "react-dom": "^19.0.0"
    },
    "catalogs": {
      "testing": {
        "jest": "30.0.0",
        "testing-library": "14.0.0"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

If you put `catalog` or `catalogs` at the top level of the `package.json` file, that will work too.

# Git Subtree Merges Summary

## Overview
A subtree merge allows you to "contain a repository within a repository" by storing a subproject in a folder of your main repository while preserving its complete Git history.

## Key Workflow

**1. Add the remote repository:**
```bash
git remote add -f spoon-knife https://github.com/octocat/Spoon-Knife.git
```

**2. Merge without committing** (prepare Git for the next step):
- Git 2.9+: `git merge -s ours --no-commit --allow-unrelated-histories spoon-knife/main`
- Git 2.8 or earlier: `git merge -s ours --no-commit spoon-knife/main`

**3. Copy the project into a subdirectory:**
```bash
git read-tree --prefix=spoon-knife/ -u spoon-knife/main
```

**4. Commit the changes:**
```bash
git commit -m "Subtree merged in spoon-knife"
```

## Keeping in Sync
Update the subproject with: `git pull -s subtree REMOTE-NAME BRANCH-NAME`

Example: `git pull -s subtree spoon-knife main`

## Important Note
Remotes added during setup won't persist in fresh clones—you'll need to re-add them using `git remote add`.

# Background Research: Hankweave Monorepo Migration

This file captures research findings, source material, and reference notes assembled during task planning for the monorepo migration.

---

## Current Repository Architecture

### Private Development Repos (what exists today)

**`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave`** (private)
- The core runtime, written in TypeScript with Bun
- Package name: `@southbridgeai/hankweave` (private npm, restricted access)
- Version: `0.5.6` as of the current snapshot
- Branch model: `develop` (active work) → `release/alpha` (customer-facing)
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `release.yml`

**`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs`** (separate repo)
- Documentation site: Next.js with Nextra 4.x
- Package name: `hankweave-docs`, version `2.0.0`
- Build: Next.js + Pagefind for search, deployed to Vercel
- No separate CI — Vercel handles builds

### Public Release Repo

**`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime`** (public)
- Receives sanitized snapshots from the private runtime via `sync-public.yml`
- Publishes the public `hankweave` npm package
- Package name: `hankweave` (public npm, accessible via `bunx hankweave` or `npx hankweave`)

---

## The Existing Cross-Repo Dependency (Key Finding)

There is already a live cross-repo dependency between `hankweave` and `hankweave-docs`.

The schema generation script at `hankweave/scripts/generate-schemas.ts` writes to two locations:
1. `hankweave/schemas/` — for the npm package
2. `../../hankweave-docs/nextra-site/public/schemas/` — for the documentation site's schema hosting

See `generate-schemas.ts:26-31`:
```typescript
const DOCS_SCHEMA_DIR = path.join(
  import.meta.dir,
  "..",
  "..",
  "hankweave-docs",
  "nextra-site",
  "public",
  "schemas",
);
```

The script silently skips writing to docs if the path doesn't exist (`docsAvailable` check at line ~77). This relative path hardcodes the assumption that both repos are checked out as siblings. A monorepo would make this relationship explicit and reliable.

---

## Current Release & Sync Pipeline

The full pipeline is:

```
SouthBridgeAI/hankweave (private, develop branch)
    ↓ scripts/release.ts (version bump, changelog, tag)
    ↓ .github/workflows/release.yml (npm publish @southbridgeai/hankweave, binaries, GH release)
    ↓ manual trigger: .github/workflows/sync-public.yml
SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime (public, release/alpha)
    ↓ public release.yml (npm publish hankweave, binaries, GH release)
```

The docs site is deployed separately to Vercel from `hankweave-docs`.

### Files Stripped Before Public Sync

From `scripts/sync-public.ts`:
- Directories: `intermediates/`, `external-docs/`, `public-release-files/`, `.github/actions/`
- Files: `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `PUBLISHING-PLAN.md`, `telemetry.md`, `scripts/sync-public.ts`, `scripts/release.ts`, `scripts/test-sync-local.ts`, `standard-operating-procedures.md`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/sync-public.yml`

The `public-release-files/` directory contains replacements overlaid on the public repo:
- `README.md` (public-facing)
- `LICENSE.md`, `NOTICE.md`
- A sanitized `reference/telemetry.md`
- A simplified `.github/workflows/release.yml`

---

## Monorepo Tooling Research

### Bun Workspaces

Bun supports the standard npm workspaces protocol natively. Configuration in root `package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "my-project",
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
```

Each package has its own `package.json`. Cross-package references use the `workspace:` protocol:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "pkg-b": "workspace:*"
  }
}
```

Key features:
- `bun install` installs all workspaces and de-duplicates dependencies
- `--filter` flag for running scripts in specific packages
- `workspace:*` replaced by real version on publish
- Bun supports full glob syntax including negative patterns
- **Catalogs**: Share common dependency versions across packages via `catalog:` protocol — define once in root, reference everywhere

**Bun workspaces are likely sufficient for this project** without adding Turborepo, since the project doesn't have many packages and build caching may not be the pain point.

### Turborepo

Turborepo adds task orchestration with caching on top of workspaces:
- `turbo.json` defines task pipelines and caching rules
- Tasks can depend on other packages' tasks (`^build` = build dependencies first)
- Significant speedup for large monorepos via remote caching
- Incremental adoption possible — can start with one task

**Turborepo may be overkill** for a two-package monorepo. Worth considering if build times become an issue, but adds complexity.

### NX

Similar to Turborepo but more opinionated. Not evaluated in depth — likely not relevant for this scale.

### Recommendation

Bun workspaces alone is the right starting point. The simplicity of two packages (runtime + docs) doesn't warrant additional tooling. Turborepo can be added later if task orchestration and caching becomes needed.

---

## Git History Preservation Options

### git subtree

Allows merging another repo into a subdirectory while preserving its commit history.

```bash
git remote add -f hankweave-docs https://github.com/SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs.git
git merge -s ours --no-commit --allow-unrelated-histories hankweave-docs/main
git read-tree --prefix=packages/docs/ -u hankweave-docs/main
git commit -m "Merge hankweave-docs into monorepo"
```

Future syncs: `git pull -s subtree hankweave-docs main`

**Downside**: Can make `git log` noisier. The merged history is preserved but the structure is complex.

### Fresh start

Create a new repo, copy files, start fresh history. Simpler but loses commit history for both repos.

### git filter-repo / grafting

More surgical — can rewrite history to place all commits in proper subdirectory paths. More complex.

**Given the project's constraints** (private dev repo, public sanitized mirror), git history preservation is "nice to have" but probably less critical than getting the structure right. The public repo already receives snapshots without full history.

---

## Key Considerations for This Migration

### 1. The Public Release Pipeline

The most complex aspect is the `develop → release/alpha → sync-to-public` pipeline. Key questions to resolve:

- Does the docs repo get a public counterpart too? Currently no.
- Does the monorepo have a single release cycle, or separate package versions?
- Does the `sync-public.ts` script need to be aware of multiple packages?

### 2. Schema Coupling

`generate-schemas.ts` already has a cross-repo dependency. In a monorepo, this becomes a proper intra-repo dependency. The `DOCS_SCHEMA_DIR` path would resolve correctly if both repos are under the same root (e.g., `packages/runtime` and `packages/docs`).

### 3. Separate npm Packages

The runtime publishes as `hankweave` (public) / `@southbridgeai/hankweave` (private). The docs site doesn't publish to npm. This is a "mixed" monorepo: one publishable package, one deployable site.

### 4. Vercel Deployment

The docs site deploys from `hankweave-docs`. Vercel supports monorepos — you specify the root directory for the project. The `vercel.json` in `nextra-site/` would need to be at the monorepo root or Vercel would need to be pointed at the subdirectory.

### 5. CI/CD Changes

The existing CI workflows are per-repo. In a monorepo:
- CI would need to run tests only for changed packages (or all)
- The release workflow for the runtime needs updating
- The docs build (currently Vercel-managed) would continue on Vercel, but with a new root path

### 6. Biome Scope

Current `biome.json` covers `server/**/*`, `tests/e2e/**/*`, `tests/utils/**/*`, `tests/unit/**/*`, `types/**/*`. In a monorepo, this would need to either: be per-package, or be a root config with includes scoped to the runtime package.

### 7. The Internal Strip Requirement

The release process strips `intermediates/`, `external-docs/`, `CLAUDE.md`, etc. from the public sync. A monorepo would need to either:
- Keep the current two-package structure where docs is a separate workspace that doesn't go through the sync
- Or ensure the sync process still correctly strips the right files

---

## Existing Intermediates That Informed Structure

The `intermediates/` directory in the hankweave repo contains planning docs for 40+ features. Most are numbered and either single files or multi-phase directories. None appear to relate to monorepo migration specifically.

Relevant to understanding how they work:
- `standard-operating-procedures.md` section 3 explains intermediates: numbered sequentially, stripped before release, visible only in private dev repo

---

## Source File Locations

| File | Path |
|------|------|
| hankweave package.json | `source/hankweave/package.json` |
| hankweave-docs package.json | `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/package.json` |
| generate-schemas.ts | `source/hankweave/scripts/generate-schemas.ts` |
| release.ts | `source/hankweave/scripts/release.ts` |
| sync-public.ts | `source/hankweave/scripts/sync-public.ts` |
| ci.yml | `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| release.yml | `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/release.yml` |
| sync-public.yml | `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/sync-public.yml` |
| biome.json | `source/hankweave/biome.json` |
| bunfig.toml | `source/hankweave/bunfig.toml` |
| standard-operating-procedures.md | `source/hankweave/standard-operating-procedures.md` |
| vercel.json | `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/vercel.json` |

---

## Research Links

- [Bun Workspaces documentation](https://bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces)
- [Bun Catalogs documentation](https://bun.sh/docs/install/catalogs)
- [Turborepo: adding to existing repo](https://turborepo.dev/repo/docs/getting-started/add-to-existing-repository)
- [GitHub: git subtree merges](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git-subtree-merges)

# Task: Migrate Hankweave to Monorepo

## Intent

From the task specification in `read_only_data_source/task.md`:

> "Migrate the Hankweave project from its current multi-repository structure into a unified monorepo. This includes the runtime (`hankweave`), documentation (`hankweave-docs`), and any related packages/tools."

The stated goals are:

> - Consolidate all Hankweave repositories into a single monorepo
> - Maintain clean package boundaries with proper workspace configuration
> - Preserve git history where practical
> - Ensure CI/CD pipelines work with the new structure
> - Keep the developer experience smooth (build, test, lint across packages)

---

## Context

### What exists today

There are currently three repos involved in the Hankweave release pipeline:

1. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave`** (private) — the core TypeScript/Bun runtime. Package `@southbridgeai/hankweave`, currently at `v0.5.6`. This is where all active development happens on a `develop → release/alpha` branch model.

2. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs`** (separate private repo) — the documentation site. Next.js + Nextra 4.x, deployed to Vercel. Package `hankweave-docs`, version `2.0.0`.

3. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime`** (public) — receives sanitized snapshots from the private runtime repo via a `sync-public` GitHub Actions workflow. Publishes the public `hankweave` npm package accessible as `bunx hankweave` / `npx hankweave`.

### The already-existing cross-repo dependency

There is a live dependency between the two dev repos that makes this migration particularly motivated: `hankweave/scripts/generate-schemas.ts` (lines 26–31) already reaches into the docs repo:

```typescript
const DOCS_SCHEMA_DIR = path.join(
  import.meta.dir, "..", "..",
  "hankweave-docs", "nextra-site", "public", "schemas",
);
```

This path hardcodes the assumption that both repos are checked out as siblings. The script silently skips writing to docs if the path doesn't exist (see `docsAvailable` check in `generate-schemas.ts`). A monorepo would make this relationship explicit and reliable rather than fragile and implicit.

### Why this task came up

The task description states: "Coordinating changes across repos creates friction - a feature that touches both runtime and docs requires multiple PRs, version bumps, and careful sequencing. A monorepo would simplify cross-cutting changes and dependency management."

The existing cross-repo schema path dependency is a concrete example of this friction — it only works if both repos happen to be checked out as siblings on a developer's machine.

---

## Why

The primary driver is developer-experience friction: documentation changes that accompany runtime feature changes require two separate PRs across two repos. The schema generation already implicitly assumes the repos are co-located. A monorepo formalizes what's already partially true.

Secondary motivations: shared tooling (Biome, TypeScript config), simplified CI, and a single place to understand the project structure.

---

## Questions

These are open questions that need answering before or during implementation. They represent the real complexity of the task.

### Q1: What happens to the public release pipeline?

The most significant open question. The current pipeline:

```
hankweave (private) → develop/release branches → sync-public → hankweave-runtime (public)
```

The docs repo (`hankweave-docs`) does **not** currently go through this pipeline. It's deployed directly to Vercel as its own repo.

In a monorepo:
- Does the monorepo have a single private → public sync, or separate ones?
- Does the docs package still deploy directly to Vercel (which supports monorepos with a root directory setting)?
- Does `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime` still exist as a separate public mirror, or does the monorepo itself become the public-facing source?
- Does `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs` cease to exist as a separate repo?

The `scripts/sync-public.ts` strips many internal files before syncing. In a monorepo, does it still only sync the runtime package, or does it need to be aware of the monorepo structure?

### Q2: What is the monorepo root structure?

Options include:
- Flat: `packages/runtime/` and `packages/docs/`
- Asymmetric: `packages/hankweave/` and `packages/hankweave-docs/` (preserving names)
- Apps-style: `packages/runtime/` and `apps/docs/` (distinguishing publishable from deployable)

The `apps/` vs `packages/` convention (used by turborepo and others) distinguishes packages that are published to npm vs. deployed apps. Since only the runtime publishes to npm, this split would be natural.

### Q3: Should a new repo be created, or should one of the existing repos be converted?

Options:
- Create a brand new `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-dev` (or similar) monorepo
- Convert `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave` to be the monorepo root (adding docs as a workspace)
- Use git subtree or filter-repo to merge history

The existing `hankweave` repo already has a clean `develop/release/alpha` branch model and the full CI infrastructure. Converting it to the monorepo root (by adding a `packages/` or keeping the runtime at root level and adding docs as `docs/`) may be the path of least resistance.

### Q4: How should the internal strip list evolve?

The `scripts/sync-public.ts` and `scripts/release.ts` both maintain lists of files to strip from the public release. In a monorepo:
- Does the strip list need to include the entire `docs/` or `apps/docs/` directory?
- Or does the sync continue to only sync the runtime package tree?
- The `intermediates/` directory (internal planning docs) is currently at the repo root. In a monorepo, does it stay at root, or move into `packages/runtime/intermediates/`?

### Q5: What changes in CI?

Currently:
- `ci.yml` runs on `develop` and `release/alpha` pushes, covering lint/typecheck, unit/integration, E2E init tests
- `release.yml` triggers on `v*` tags, publishing npm and building binaries
- `sync-public.yml` is manually triggered for public sync
- Vercel handles docs deployment

In a monorepo, CI should ideally only run the relevant jobs when specific packages change (using path filtering). This is where Turborepo or similar would add value — but path filtering in GitHub Actions is already supported via `paths` triggers without additional tooling.

### Q6: How does Vercel handle the docs site in a monorepo?

Vercel supports monorepos by letting you specify the "Root Directory" in the project settings. The current `vercel.json` in `nextra-site/` would need to be at the correct location relative to the monorepo root, or the Vercel project would need to be reconfigured to point to `apps/docs/nextra-site/` (or wherever docs lands).

### Q7: What's the versioning strategy?

The runtime is versioned independently (`0.5.6`). The docs site is `2.0.0` (and doesn't publish to npm). In a monorepo:
- Does each package have independent versions (current approach)?
- Or is there a synchronized monorepo-wide version?

Independent versioning is almost certainly correct here: the runtime and docs don't release in lockstep, and the runtime is the thing with semver meaning for users.

### Q8: Should the new monorepo have a `workspace:*` dependency from docs to runtime?

If the docs site ever needs to import from the runtime (e.g., for auto-generated API reference, schema validation in docs, etc.), a `workspace:*` dependency would make this possible. Currently, the only cross-package dependency is the schema sync in `generate-schemas.ts`. Whether to formalize this as a proper workspace dependency or keep it as a script-level path reference is a decision to make.

---

## Research

### Bun Workspaces

Bun natively supports workspaces via the standard `workspaces` field in `package.json`. For a two-package monorepo:

```json
{
  "name": "hankweave-dev",
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
```

Cross-package dependencies use the `workspace:` protocol: `"workspace:*"`. Bun's **Catalogs** feature allows sharing dependency versions across packages via a `catalog:` protocol — useful for ensuring runtime and docs use the same version of shared tools like TypeScript.

Bun is fast enough (reportedly 28x faster than npm) that the build-caching features of Turborepo may not be needed.

See: [Bun Workspaces docs](https://bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces), [Bun Catalogs docs](https://bun.sh/docs/install/catalogs)

### Turborepo

Turborepo adds task orchestration and caching on top of workspaces. A `turbo.json` defines task pipelines with dependency ordering. For a two-package monorepo, this is likely overkill — but can be added later if build times become a concern.

See: [Turborepo: add to existing repo](https://turborepo.dev/repo/docs/getting-started/add-to-existing-repository)

### Git History Preservation

`git subtree add` can merge another repo into a subdirectory while preserving history. The approach:

```bash
git remote add -f hankweave-docs <url>
git merge -s ours --no-commit --allow-unrelated-histories hankweave-docs/main
git read-tree --prefix=apps/docs/ -u hankweave-docs/main
git commit -m "Merge hankweave-docs into monorepo"
```

Given that the public repo (`hankweave-runtime`) already receives snapshots without full history, and the docs repo has no complex history of its own, preserving history may be "nice to have" but not critical. A fresh start would be simpler.

See: [GitHub: git subtree merges](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git-subtree-merges)

---

## References

### Code References

| Item | Location |
|------|----------|
| hankweave `package.json` | `source/hankweave/package.json:1-98` |
| hankweave-docs `package.json` | `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/package.json` |
| Cross-repo schema path (key finding) | `source/hankweave/scripts/generate-schemas.ts:26-31` |
| Release script (branch model, strip list) | `source/hankweave/scripts/release.ts` |
| Sync-to-public script | `source/hankweave/scripts/sync-public.ts` |
| Standard operating procedures | `source/hankweave/standard-operating-procedures.md` |
| CI workflow | `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| Release workflow | `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/release.yml` |
| Sync-public workflow | `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/sync-public.yml` |
| Biome config | `source/hankweave/biome.json` |
| Vercel config | `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/vercel.json` |
| Bun config | `source/hankweave/bunfig.toml` |

### Background Material

All research findings are compiled in `plan/background/background.md`.

### Key Observation from Source

From `standard-operating-procedures.md`, section 1 (Repository Structure):

> "There is a separate public repo at `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime` which receives sanitized snapshots via the sync workflow. It publishes the public `hankweave` npm package."

This is the "one-way door" that the AI agent policy section references. Any monorepo migration needs to preserve or replace this pipeline carefully.

From `standard-operating-procedures.md`, section 11 (AI Agent Policy):

> "**Running `scripts/sync-public.ts` or `scripts/test-sync-local.ts --push`** — agents must never execute the sync to the public repo."

This is relevant context for the migration work itself — the migration plan and any scripts need to be careful about the public sync boundary.

---

## Additional Notes

### What is NOT in scope (inferred)

Based on the task description, these appear to be non-goals:
- Merging `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime` (the public mirror) into the monorepo — it's a downstream artifact, not a development repo
- Creating a public monorepo (the separation between private dev and public release appears intentional and valuable)
- Adding entirely new packages beyond runtime and docs

### The "tools" question

The task mentions "any related packages/tools." The `tools/linear-pull` directory in the agent workspace is a separate utility, not part of the hankweave source. Within the hankweave repo, the `scripts/`, `shims/`, and `schemas/` directories are part of the runtime package, not separate packages.

There's no immediate evidence of standalone "tools" packages that would need to be separate workspaces — but this warrants a direct question to the human owner.

### Vercel deployment specifics

The current `vercel.json` in `nextra-site/` points to a Next.js app with a custom build command. Vercel supports monorepos by configuring a "Root Directory" in the project dashboard. After the migration, the Vercel project for docs would need to be pointed at `apps/docs/nextra-site` (or wherever the docs site lands). The `vercel.json` itself stays in the same location relative to the Next.js project root.

### The `standard-operating-procedures.md` branch model implication

The current SOP says:
> "feature branches → develop → release/alpha"

In a monorepo, this branch model could stay the same (one `develop` branch for all packages) or could be split (separate release cadences per package). Given the scale (two packages), keeping a single branch model is almost certainly right.

# Task: Migrate Hankweave to Monorepo

## Intent

From the task specification in `read_only_data_source/task.md`:

> "Migrate the Hankweave project from its current multi-repository structure into a unified monorepo. This includes the runtime (`hankweave`), documentation (`hankweave-docs`), and any related packages/tools."

The stated goals are:

> - Consolidate all Hankweave repositories into a single monorepo
> - Maintain clean package boundaries with proper workspace configuration
> - Preserve git history where practical
> - Ensure CI/CD pipelines work with the new structure
> - Keep the developer experience smooth (build, test, lint across packages)

Stated considerations from the task spec:

> - Bun workspaces vs other monorepo tooling (turborepo, nx, etc.)
> - Package publishing strategy (npm packages from monorepo)
> - Schema sharing between packages
> - Test infrastructure consolidation
> - Documentation site build integration
> - Binary build pipeline for cross-platform releases

---

## Context

### What exists today

There are currently three repos involved in the Hankweave release pipeline:

1. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave`** (private) — the core TypeScript/Bun runtime. Package `@southbridgeai/hankweave`, currently at `v0.5.6`. All active development happens here on a `develop → release/alpha` branch model.

2. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs`** (separate private repo) — the documentation site. Next.js + Nextra 4.x, deployed to Vercel. Package name `hankweave-docs`, version `2.0.0`.

3. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime`** (public) — receives sanitized snapshots from the private runtime repo via a `sync-public` GitHub Actions workflow. Publishes the public `hankweave` npm package accessible as `bunx hankweave` / `npx hankweave`.

### The already-existing cross-repo dependency (key finding)

There is a live implicit dependency between the two dev repos that makes this migration particularly motivated: `hankweave/scripts/generate-schemas.ts` (lines 26–31) already reaches into the docs repo:

```typescript
const DOCS_SCHEMA_DIR = path.join(
  import.meta.dir, "..", "..",
  "hankweave-docs", "nextra-site", "public", "schemas",
);
```

This path hardcodes the assumption that both repos are checked out as siblings. The script silently skips writing to docs if the path doesn't exist. A monorepo would make this relationship explicit and reliable rather than fragile and implicit.

### Why this came up

The task description states: "Coordinating changes across repos creates friction - a feature that touches both runtime and docs requires multiple PRs, version bumps, and careful sequencing. A monorepo would simplify cross-cutting changes and dependency management."

The schema generation dependency is a concrete example of that friction — it only works if both repos happen to be checked out side-by-side on a developer's machine.

### Is there related existing work?

No monorepo-related intermediates were found in `source/hankweave/intermediates/`. The existing planning docs (numbered up to 44) cover other feature areas. This appears to be a net-new task.

No Linear ticket ID was present in the task data source. The project uses `ENG-` prefixes for Linear tickets (visible in the CHANGELOG and PR titles). This task may have a ticket, but it wasn't included in the provided data.

---

## Why

The primary driver is developer-experience friction from coordinating changes across two repos. The schema generation already implicitly assumes the repos are co-located — a monorepo formalizes what's already partially true.

Secondary motivations: shared tooling (Biome config, TypeScript, Bun), simplified CI path filtering, and a single place to understand the full project structure. With a monorepo, a PR that adds a new runtime feature and updates its documentation can be a single atomic change.

---

## Questions

These are open questions that need answering before or during implementation. They represent the real complexity of this task.

### Q1: What happens to the public release pipeline?

The most significant open question. The current pipeline is:

```
hankweave (private dev repo) → sync-public workflow → hankweave-runtime (public mirror)
```

The docs repo (`hankweave-docs`) does **not** go through this pipeline. It deploys directly to Vercel.

In a monorepo:
- Does the monorepo have a single private → public sync, or separate ones per package?
- Does the docs package still deploy directly from the monorepo to Vercel (Vercel supports this with root directory configuration)?
- Does `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime` still exist as a separate public mirror, or does the monorepo eventually become the public-facing source?
- Does `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs` cease to exist as an independent repo?

The `scripts/sync-public.ts` strips many internal files before syncing. In a monorepo, the sync probably continues to only push the runtime package tree — but the strip list may need to account for the new directory structure.

### Q2: What is the monorepo root structure?

Options include:
- Flat: `packages/runtime/` and `packages/docs/`
- Named: `packages/hankweave/` and `packages/hankweave-docs/`
- Apps-style: `packages/hankweave/` and `apps/docs/` (distinguishing publishable from deployable)

The `apps/` vs `packages/` convention (common in Turborepo docs) distinguishes npm-publishable packages from deployable apps. Since only the runtime publishes to npm, this split would be natural. But it also adds a directory depth that may not be worth it for two packages.

The question of whether the runtime stays at the repo root or moves into a subdirectory is also open. Keeping the runtime at root with docs in `docs/` is the minimal-disruption approach.

### Q3: Should a new repo be created, or should an existing one be converted?

Options:
- **Create a new repo** (e.g., `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-dev`) and bring both repos in
- **Convert `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave`** to be the monorepo root (add docs as a workspace, minimal disruption to existing CI/release infrastructure)
- **Use git subtree** to merge docs history into the runtime repo as a subdirectory

Converting the runtime repo to be the monorepo root is the lowest-friction path: all CI workflows, secrets, branch protection rules, and Linear integrations stay in place.

### Q4: What changes in the internal strip list?

`scripts/release.ts` and `scripts/sync-public.ts` both maintain lists of files/directories to strip before the public sync:
- `intermediates/`, `external-docs/`, `public-release-files/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, etc.

In a monorepo, the docs workspace (wherever it lands) is also internal-only and should not appear in the public runtime snapshot. The strip list needs updating.

### Q5: What changes in CI?

Currently:
- `ci.yml` runs on `develop` and `release/alpha` pushes: lint/typecheck, unit/integration tests, E2E init tests
- `release.yml` triggers on `v*` tags: npm publish + binary builds
- `sync-public.yml` manually triggered for public sync
- Vercel handles docs deployment separately

In a monorepo, CI should ideally only run relevant jobs for changed packages. GitHub Actions supports path filtering with `paths:` triggers. The question is how granular to make this — for two packages, running everything on every push may still be acceptable.

### Q6: How does Vercel handle the docs site in a monorepo?

Vercel supports monorepos by letting you specify the "Root Directory" in project settings. The current `vercel.json` in `nextra-site/` would stay in place relative to the Next.js project root. The Vercel project would need to be reconfigured to point to the new path (e.g., `apps/docs/nextra-site/` or `docs/nextra-site/`).

### Q7: Versioning strategy?

The runtime is versioned independently (`0.5.6`). The docs site is `2.0.0` and doesn't publish to npm. Independent versioning per package is almost certainly correct — the runtime and docs don't release in lockstep, and semver on the runtime is meaningful for users while the docs version is internal.

### Q8: Should `workspace:*` link docs to runtime?

If the docs site ever needs to import from the runtime (e.g., for auto-generated API reference or schema types), a `workspace:*` dependency would make this a proper workspace dependency. Currently the only cross-package dependency is a path-based write in `generate-schemas.ts`. Whether to formalize this as a workspace dependency or keep it as a script-level path reference is a decision point.

### Q9: What is the scope of "related packages/tools"?

The task mentions "any related packages/tools." The `tools/linear-pull` in this agent workspace is a planning utility, not part of the hankweave source. Within the hankweave repo, `scripts/`, `shims/`, and `schemas/` are part of the runtime package, not separate packages. It's worth confirming with the task author whether there are any other tools or packages not visible in the current source snapshot.

---

## Research

### Bun Workspaces

Bun natively supports workspaces via the standard `workspaces` field in `package.json`. For a two-package monorepo:

```json
{
  "name": "hankweave-dev",
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
```

Cross-package references use the `workspace:` protocol (`"workspace:*"`). Bun's **Catalogs** feature shares dependency versions across packages via `catalog:` protocol — useful for ensuring runtime and docs agree on shared tools like TypeScript.

Full docs: [bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces](https://bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces), [bun.sh/docs/install/catalogs](https://bun.sh/docs/install/catalogs)

### Turborepo

Turborepo adds task orchestration and caching on top of workspaces. A `turbo.json` defines task pipelines with dependency ordering (`^build` = build dependencies first). For a two-package monorepo, this is likely overkill initially — but can be adopted incrementally. Worth noting: Turborepo supports incremental adoption, meaning you can start with one task and expand.

Full docs: [turborepo.dev/repo/docs/getting-started/add-to-existing-repository](https://turborepo.dev/repo/docs/getting-started/add-to-existing-repository)

### Git History Preservation

`git subtree add` can merge another repo into a subdirectory while preserving its full commit history:

```bash
git remote add -f hankweave-docs <url>
git merge -s ours --no-commit --allow-unrelated-histories hankweave-docs/main
git read-tree --prefix=apps/docs/ -u hankweave-docs/main
git commit -m "Merge hankweave-docs into monorepo"
```

Given that `hankweave-runtime` (public mirror) already receives snapshots without full history, and the docs repo has no complex history of its own, preserving history is "nice to have" but not critical.

Full docs: [docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git-subtree-merges](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git-subtree-merges)

# Task: Migrate Hankweave to Monorepo

## Intent

From the task specification in `read_only_data_source/task.md`:

> "Migrate the Hankweave project from its current multi-repository structure into a unified monorepo. This includes the runtime (`hankweave`), documentation (`hankweave-docs`), and any related packages/tools."

The stated goals are:

> - Consolidate all Hankweave repositories into a single monorepo
> - Maintain clean package boundaries with proper workspace configuration
> - Preserve git history where practical
> - Ensure CI/CD pipelines work with the new structure
> - Keep the developer experience smooth (build, test, lint across packages)

Stated considerations from the task spec:

> - Bun workspaces vs other monorepo tooling (turborepo, nx, etc.)
> - Package publishing strategy (npm packages from monorepo)
> - Schema sharing between packages
> - Test infrastructure consolidation
> - Documentation site build integration
> - Binary build pipeline for cross-platform releases

---

## Context

### What exists today

There are currently three repos involved in the Hankweave release pipeline:

1. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave`** (private) — the core TypeScript/Bun runtime. Package `@southbridgeai/hankweave`, currently at `v0.5.6`. All active development happens here on a `develop → release/alpha` branch model.

2. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs`** (separate private repo) — the documentation site. Next.js + Nextra 4.x, deployed to Vercel. Package name `hankweave-docs`, version `2.0.0`.

3. **`SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime`** (public) — receives sanitized snapshots from the private runtime repo via a `sync-public` GitHub Actions workflow. Publishes the public `hankweave` npm package accessible as `bunx hankweave` / `npx hankweave`.

### The already-existing cross-repo dependency (key finding)

There is a live implicit dependency between the two dev repos that makes this migration particularly motivated: `hankweave/scripts/generate-schemas.ts` (lines 26–31) already reaches into the docs repo:

```typescript
const DOCS_SCHEMA_DIR = path.join(
  import.meta.dir, "..", "..",
  "hankweave-docs", "nextra-site", "public", "schemas",
);
```

This path hardcodes the assumption that both repos are checked out as siblings. The script silently skips writing to docs if the path doesn't exist. A monorepo would make this relationship explicit and reliable rather than fragile and implicit.

### Why this came up

The task description states: "Coordinating changes across repos creates friction - a feature that touches both runtime and docs requires multiple PRs, version bumps, and careful sequencing. A monorepo would simplify cross-cutting changes and dependency management."

The schema generation dependency is a concrete example of that friction — it only works if both repos happen to be checked out side-by-side on a developer's machine.

### Is there related existing work?

No monorepo-related intermediates were found in `source/hankweave/intermediates/`. The existing planning docs (numbered up to 44) cover other feature areas. This appears to be a net-new task.

No Linear ticket ID was present in the task data source. The project uses `ENG-` prefixes for Linear tickets (visible in the CHANGELOG and PR titles). This task may have a ticket, but it wasn't included in the provided data.

---

## Why

The primary driver is developer-experience friction from coordinating changes across two repos. The schema generation already implicitly assumes the repos are co-located — a monorepo formalizes what's already partially true.

Secondary motivations: shared tooling (Biome config, TypeScript, Bun), simplified CI path filtering, and a single place to understand the full project structure. With a monorepo, a PR that adds a new runtime feature and updates its documentation can be a single atomic change.

---

## Questions

These are open questions that need answering before or during implementation. They represent the real complexity of this task.

### Q1: What happens to the public release pipeline?

The most significant open question. The current pipeline is:

```
hankweave (private dev repo) → sync-public workflow → hankweave-runtime (public mirror)
```

The docs repo (`hankweave-docs`) does **not** go through this pipeline. It deploys directly to Vercel.

In a monorepo:
- Does the monorepo have a single private → public sync, or separate ones per package?
- Does the docs package still deploy directly from the monorepo to Vercel (Vercel supports this with root directory configuration)?
- Does `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime` still exist as a separate public mirror, or does the monorepo eventually become the public-facing source?
- Does `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs` cease to exist as an independent repo?

The `scripts/sync-public.ts` strips many internal files before syncing. In a monorepo, the sync probably continues to only push the runtime package tree — but the strip list may need to account for the new directory structure.

### Q2: What is the monorepo root structure?

Options include:
- Flat: `packages/runtime/` and `packages/docs/`
- Named: `packages/hankweave/` and `packages/hankweave-docs/`
- Apps-style: `packages/hankweave/` and `apps/docs/` (distinguishing publishable from deployable)

The `apps/` vs `packages/` convention (common in Turborepo docs) distinguishes npm-publishable packages from deployable apps. Since only the runtime publishes to npm, this split would be natural. But it also adds a directory depth that may not be worth it for two packages.

The question of whether the runtime stays at the repo root or moves into a subdirectory is also open. Keeping the runtime at root with docs in `docs/` is the minimal-disruption approach.

### Q3: Should a new repo be created, or should an existing one be converted?

Options:
- **Create a new repo** (e.g., `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-dev`) and bring both repos in
- **Convert `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave`** to be the monorepo root (add docs as a workspace, minimal disruption to existing CI/release infrastructure)
- **Use git subtree** to merge docs history into the runtime repo as a subdirectory

Converting the runtime repo to be the monorepo root is the lowest-friction path: all CI workflows, secrets, branch protection rules, and Linear integrations stay in place.

### Q4: What changes in the internal strip list?

`scripts/release.ts` and `scripts/sync-public.ts` both maintain lists of files/directories to strip before the public sync:
- `intermediates/`, `external-docs/`, `public-release-files/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, etc.

In a monorepo, the docs workspace (wherever it lands) is also internal-only and should not appear in the public runtime snapshot. The strip list needs updating.

### Q5: What changes in CI?

Currently:
- `ci.yml` runs on `develop` and `release/alpha` pushes: lint/typecheck, unit/integration tests, E2E init tests
- `release.yml` triggers on `v*` tags: npm publish + binary builds
- `sync-public.yml` manually triggered for public sync
- Vercel handles docs deployment separately

In a monorepo, CI should ideally only run relevant jobs for changed packages. GitHub Actions supports path filtering with `paths:` triggers. The question is how granular to make this — for two packages, running everything on every push may still be acceptable.

### Q6: How does Vercel handle the docs site in a monorepo?

Vercel supports monorepos by letting you specify the "Root Directory" in project settings. The current `vercel.json` in `nextra-site/` would stay in place relative to the Next.js project root. The Vercel project would need to be reconfigured to point to the new path (e.g., `apps/docs/nextra-site/` or `docs/nextra-site/`).

### Q7: Versioning strategy?

The runtime is versioned independently (`0.5.6`). The docs site is `2.0.0` and doesn't publish to npm. Independent versioning per package is almost certainly correct — the runtime and docs don't release in lockstep, and semver on the runtime is meaningful for users while the docs version is internal.

### Q8: Should `workspace:*` link docs to runtime?

If the docs site ever needs to import from the runtime (e.g., for auto-generated API reference or schema types), a `workspace:*` dependency would make this a proper workspace dependency. Currently the only cross-package dependency is a path-based write in `generate-schemas.ts`. Whether to formalize this as a workspace dependency or keep it as a script-level path reference is a decision point.

### Q9: What is the scope of "related packages/tools"?

The task mentions "any related packages/tools." The `tools/linear-pull` in this agent workspace is a planning utility, not part of the hankweave source. Within the hankweave repo, `scripts/`, `shims/`, and `schemas/` are part of the runtime package, not separate packages. It's worth confirming with the task author whether there are any other tools or packages not visible in the current source snapshot.

---

## Research

### Bun Workspaces

Bun natively supports workspaces via the standard `workspaces` field in `package.json`. For a two-package monorepo:

```json
{
  "name": "hankweave-dev",
  "workspaces": ["packages/*"]
}
```

Cross-package references use the `workspace:` protocol (`"workspace:*"`). Bun's **Catalogs** feature shares dependency versions across packages via `catalog:` protocol — useful for ensuring runtime and docs agree on shared tools like TypeScript.

Full docs: [bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces](https://bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces), [bun.sh/docs/install/catalogs](https://bun.sh/docs/install/catalogs)

### Turborepo

Turborepo adds task orchestration and caching on top of workspaces. A `turbo.json` defines task pipelines with dependency ordering (`^build` = build dependencies first). For a two-package monorepo, this is likely overkill initially — but can be adopted incrementally. Worth noting: Turborepo supports incremental adoption, meaning you can start with one task and expand.

Full docs: [turborepo.dev/repo/docs/getting-started/add-to-existing-repository](https://turborepo.dev/repo/docs/getting-started/add-to-existing-repository)

### Git History Preservation

`git subtree add` can merge another repo into a subdirectory while preserving its full commit history:

```bash
git remote add -f hankweave-docs <url>
git merge -s ours --no-commit --allow-unrelated-histories hankweave-docs/main
git read-tree --prefix=apps/docs/ -u hankweave-docs/main
git commit -m "Merge hankweave-docs into monorepo"
```

Given that `hankweave-runtime` (public mirror) already receives snapshots without full history, and the docs repo has no complex history of its own, preserving history is "nice to have" but not critical.

Full docs: [docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git-subtree-merges](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git-subtree-merges)

---

## References

### Code references

| Release script | `source/hankweave/scripts/release.ts` | Branch model, strip list |

1→# Meet Hankweave 
     2→
     3→
     4→The official documentation for Hankweave—a runtime for reliable, brownfield AI engineering.

     6→These docs were built by Hankweave. So were the diagrams.

    10→---
    11→
    12→## What is Hankweave?
    13→
    14→Hankweave freezes ephemeral agentic behaviors into declarative, reproducible programs. When your agent fails on run #47, you don't debug "emergent behavior." You trace the exact sequence of events, roll back to a checkpoint, and fix it.
    15→
    16→The core abstraction is the **codon**—an atomic unit of agent work with a prompt, a model, and tracked files. Codons sequence into **hanks** (JSON programs). Between codons, you get git checkpoints, event logs, and clear boundaries. Problems in codon 3 don't leak into codon 7.
    17→
    18→For the full picture, start with [Codons](/concepts/codons) and [Hanks](/concepts/hanks).

    23→
    24→The documentation is organized into four sections:
    25→

    28→| **Guides** | Step-by-step tutorials—start here if you're new |

# Planning Log: Hankweave Monorepo Migration

## Areas Read

- [x] source/hankweave/server - core runtime code (60+ .ts files, well-organized subdirs)
- [x] source/hankweave/package.json - @southbridgeai/hankweave v0.5.6, Bun runtime, many scripts
- [x] source/hankweave/scripts/ - build.ts, build-executable.ts, release.ts, sync-public.ts, generate-schemas.ts, e2e/init.ts, run-cross-runtime-tests.ts, test-sync-local.ts
- [x] source/hankweave/.github/workflows/ - ci.yml, release.yml, sync-public.yml
- [x] source/hankweave/.github/actions/ - setup-environment, run-tests, dump-test-logs (composite actions)
- [x] source/hankweave/biome.json - covers server/, tests/e2e/, tests/utils/, tests/unit/, types/
- [x] source/hankweave/bunfig.toml - minimal, just BUN_TEST env var for tests
- [x] source/hankweave/tsconfig.json - ES2022, strict, bun-types
- [x] source/hankweave/.gitignore, .npmignore, .gitattributes
- [x] source/hankweave/standard-operating-procedures.md - comprehensive SOPs
- [x] source/hankweave-docs/ - Nextra 4, Next.js 15, Bun install+build
- [x] source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/package.json - hankweave-docs v2.0.0
- [x] source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/vercel.json - framework: nextjs, bun install/build
- [x] source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/tsconfig.json - ES2020, strict:false, bundler resolution
- [x] source/hankweave/tests/ - 65+ unit tests, 10+ integration, 10+ e2e, cross-runtime tests
- [x] plan/background/background.md - pre-compiled research

## Aha Moments

### 1. The docs project has a nested structure
The docs repo is `hankweave-docs/` at root but the actual Next.js project is at `hankweave-docs/nextra-site/`. The `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `next.config.mjs` etc. are all inside `nextra-site/`. The docs repo root has `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `notes/`, `plan/`.

This means that wherever docs lands in the monorepo, you need to decide: does the workspace point to the `nextra-site/` subdirectory (where package.json lives), or to the outer `hankweave-docs/` directory?

**Decision**: The workspace should point to where `package.json` is — so the `nextra-site/` level. The outer `hankweave-docs/` scaffold (README, notes, plan) is development overhead that probably doesn't need its own workspace and can either be flattened or kept as-is.

### 2. generate-schemas.ts is the only real cross-repo code reference
Grep confirms only `scripts/generate-schemas.ts:28` references `hankweave-docs` in actual code. All other references are in `intermediates/` planning documents (which are stripped on release). This simplifies the migration — only one file needs a path adjustment.

### 3. The docs have NO dependency on the runtime package
The docs site (`hankweave-docs`) doesn't `import` anything from `@southbridgeai/hankweave`. The only cross-repo data flow is schemas generated by the runtime and written to the docs `public/schemas/` directory. A `workspace:*` dependency is NOT needed at this time.

### 4. The public sync pipeline only needs to export the runtime
The `sync-public.ts` script works from the root of the hankweave repo. In a monorepo, if the runtime stays at the root, the sync script barely changes. If it moves into a subdirectory, the strip lists and snapshot process need reworking.

### 5. CI uses composite actions with relative paths
All three composite actions (`.github/actions/*`) are referenced as `./.github/actions/setup-environment` etc. These use relative paths. As long as the `.github/` directory stays at the monorepo root, they work. The composite actions themselves just do `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun test` — they'd work with workspaces too.

### 6. The release script assumes it runs from the repo root
`release.ts` uses `resolve(process.cwd())` for paths and runs `git` commands. It also runs `bun run generate-schemas` and `bun run tc`. These all assume the cwd is the package root. In a monorepo with the runtime as a workspace, scripts would need to be run from the workspace directory or paths adjusted.

### 7. build.ts uses relative paths from import.meta.dir
`build.ts` resolves `distDir` as `join(import.meta.dir, "..", "dist")` and entry point as `"./server/index.ts"`. This means build.ts must run from (or be relative to) the runtime package root. Same for `build-executable.ts`.

### 8. Vercel monorepo support just needs "Root Directory"
Vercel lets you set the "Root Directory" for a project in project settings. The current `vercel.json` in `nextra-site/` would work if Vercel is pointed at the right subdirectory. This is a settings change, not a code change.

### 9. The docs package.json has a `postbuild` step
`"postbuild": "pagefind --site .next/server/app --output-path public/_pagefind"` — this runs Pagefind after `next build`. This would work fine in a workspace since `next build` runs from the workspace directory.

### 10. tsconfig.json settings differ significantly between the two projects
- Runtime: `target: ES2022`, `module: ES2022`, `moduleResolution: node`, `strict: true`, types: `bun-types`
- Docs: `target: ES2020`, `module: esnext`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, `strict: false`, plugins: `next`

These configs should NOT be shared. Each workspace needs its own `tsconfig.json`.

### 11. There's only one bun.lock file per project
Currently `source/hankweave/bun.lock` and `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/bun.lock`. In a monorepo, there would be a single root-level `bun.lock` file managed by Bun workspaces.

### 12. The runtime's `.npmignore` strips `server/`, `scripts/`, `tests/` for npm publish
npm publish only includes `dist/`, `shims/`, `schemas/`. This is controlled by both `.npmignore` and the `"files"` field in `package.json`. In a monorepo, the npm publish command would need to run from the runtime workspace. `"files"` field should continue to work correctly.

## Key Decision Points

### Structure Decision: Runtime at root vs in a subdirectory

**Option A: Runtime stays at repo root, docs moves in as a workspace**
```
hankweave/                  (monorepo root = runtime package root)
├── package.json            (root package.json with workspaces field, ALSO the runtime)
├── server/
├── scripts/
├── tests/
├── docs/                   (was: hankweave-docs/nextra-site)
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── app/
│   ├── content/
│   └── ...
└── ...
```
- Pro: Minimal disruption to existing paths, scripts, CI
- Pro: All existing relative paths in server/scripts still work
- Con: The root package.json serves dual purpose (workspace root AND runtime package)
- Con: `bun install` at root installs both workspace deps — might be slightly confusing

**Option B: Both packages in subdirectories**
```
hankweave/                  (monorepo root)
├── package.json            (workspace root, not a package itself)
├── packages/
│   ├── runtime/            (was: hankweave root)
│   │   ├── package.json
│   │   ├── server/
│   │   └── ...
│   └── docs/               (was: hankweave-docs/nextra-site)
│       ├── package.json
│       └── ...
└── .github/
```
- Pro: Clean separation, conventional monorepo structure
- Con: MASSIVE amount of path changes — every script, CI workflow, build config, `import.meta.dir` reference
- Con: git history gets complicated
- Con: The release.ts, sync-public.ts, build.ts all need significant reworking

**Option C: Runtime at root, docs as apps/docs**
```
hankweave/                  (monorepo root = runtime package root)
├── package.json            (root + runtime)
├── server/
├── apps/
│   └── docs/               (was: hankweave-docs/nextra-site)
│       ├── package.json
│       └── ...
└── ...
```
- Pro: Distinguishes "apps" (deployable) from packages (publishable) — common Turborepo pattern
- Con: `apps/` is a Turborepo convention that might be overengineering for two packages
- Otherwise similar to Option A

### Recommendation: Option A (runtime at root)

The path of least disruption. The runtime is the primary package — it has the most scripts, CI workflows, and tooling built around its position at root. Moving it into a subdirectory would require changing dozens of paths across scripts, workflows, and configs.

The docs site is the smaller, simpler addition. Putting it at `docs/` (or `docs/nextra-site/`) within the runtime's repo structure is the minimal change.

The trade-off: the root `package.json` serves double duty. But Bun workspaces handles this fine — you can have `"workspaces": ["docs"]` in the root and the root itself is also a package.

### Sync-public impact

With Option A (runtime at root), the sync-public.ts barely changes. The only new item is that the `docs/` directory needs to be added to the `STRIP_DIRS` list so it doesn't end up in the public runtime snapshot. Everything else stays the same.

### CI impact

With Option A:
- `ci.yml` barely changes — the runtime is still at root, `bun install` installs all workspaces, tests run from root
- `release.yml` same thing
- Optional: Add path filtering so docs-only changes skip runtime tests (nice to have, not required initially)

### generate-schemas.ts impact

The `DOCS_SCHEMA_DIR` path changes from `../../hankweave-docs/nextra-site/public/schemas` to `../docs/public/schemas` (one level up from `scripts/`, then into `docs/`). This is actually simpler.

## Questions Resolved

1. **Full directory structure** — mapped exhaustively
2. **Script invocation** — all via `bun run <script>` or `bun scripts/<file>.ts`
3. **Sync-public strips** — STRIP_DIRS + STRIP_FILES documented, understood
4. **Test infrastructure** — bun:test, 65+ unit, 10+ integration, e2e with mock LLMs
5. **server/ depth** — 3-4 levels (server/sentinels/, server/llm/, server/types/, etc.)
6. **Docs structure** — Nextra 4 + Next.js 15, content/ for MDX, app/ for routes, components/ for custom

## Questions Remaining

1. **Should the outer hankweave-docs/ wrapper be kept?** — The docs repo has a root-level README, notes/, plan/ directory outside nextra-site/. These are dev-only files. Probably flatten: just bring nextra-site/ contents into docs/.
2. **Shared dev dependencies?** — Both projects use TypeScript. The docs use `@types/node` and `@types/react`. The runtime uses `@types/bun`. Bun catalogs could share TypeScript version, but it's not critical.
3. **Does the monorepo need its own README at root?** — The current runtime README is internal. The public one is in `public-release-files/`. Adding a monorepo root README could be helpful but isn't strictly necessary for the migration.

# Plan: Migrate Hankweave to Monorepo

## a. The Main Task

Consolidate the `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave` (runtime) and `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-docs` (documentation site) repositories into a single monorepo using Bun workspaces. The runtime package stays at the repository root; the docs site moves in as a workspace at `docs/`. The existing CI/CD pipelines, release process, and public sync workflow continue to function with minimal changes.

---

## b. Information Available

### Sources that informed this plan

1. **Task specification** — `plan/task.md` (the task description, open questions, and research)
2. **Background research** — `plan/background/background.md` (Bun workspace docs, Turborepo evaluation, git subtree options)
3. **Full source code** — Read every config, script, workflow, and representative server/test files from both repos
4. **SOP document** — `source/hankweave/standard-operating-procedures.md` (branch model, release process, AI agent policy)

### What I could see

- Full directory structure and file contents of both `source/hankweave/` and `source/hankweave-docs/`
- All CI workflows, composite actions, and build/release/sync scripts
- Test infrastructure (patterns, paths, utilities, config fixtures)
- Both `package.json` files, `tsconfig.json` files, `biome.json`, `bunfig.toml`
- The docs Nextra/Next.js setup including `vercel.json`, `next.config.mjs`, `app/`, `content/`

### What I could NOT see

- The actual `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave-runtime` (public mirror) repo — only references to it in scripts and workflows
- Vercel project settings (the current "Root Directory" config for docs deployment)
- GitHub repo settings (branch protection rules, secrets configuration)
- Linear project (no ticket ID was provided)
- Whether there are any other repositories or tools the task spec's "related packages/tools" refers to beyond what's in the source snapshot

### Assumptions made

1. The `hankweave-docs` repo has no significant git history worth preserving (the task says "nice to have" for history)
2. The public mirror (`hankweave-runtime`) continues to exist as a separate repo — this migration consolidates the two **private development** repos
3. The docs site continues to deploy to Vercel from the same repo (now a monorepo)
4. No Turborepo or other task orchestration is needed for two packages

---

## c. Sources and Related Things

### Original tickets/tasks

- Task description: `plan/task.md`
- No Linear ticket ID provided

### Code references

| File | Line(s) | Relevance |
|------|---------|-----------|
| `source/hankweave/package.json` | Full | Root package.json — needs `workspaces` field added |
| `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/package.json` | Full | Docs package.json — moves to `docs/package.json` |
| `source/hankweave/scripts/generate-schemas.ts` | 24-32 | The only cross-repo code dependency; path to docs schemas dir |
| `source/hankweave/scripts/sync-public.ts` | 28-44 | STRIP_DIRS/STRIP_FILES — needs `docs` added to strip list |
| `source/hankweave/scripts/release.ts` | 54-60 | INTERNAL_FILES_TO_STRIP — needs `docs/` added |
| `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Full | CI workflow — minimal changes needed |
| `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/release.yml` | Full | Release workflow — minimal changes |
| `source/hankweave/.github/workflows/sync-public.yml` | Full | Sync workflow — minimal changes |
| `source/hankweave/.github/actions/setup-environment/action.yml` | Full | Composite action — `bun install` already handles workspaces |
| `source/hankweave/biome.json` | Full | Linting scope — currently only covers runtime files |
| `source/hankweave/bunfig.toml` | Full | Bun config — no changes needed |
| `source/hankweave/tsconfig.json` | Full | Runtime TypeScript config — stays as-is |
| `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/tsconfig.json` | Full | Docs TypeScript config — stays as-is in new location |
| `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/vercel.json` | Full | Vercel config — stays in docs workspace |
| `source/hankweave-docs/nextra-site/next.config.mjs` | Full | Next.js config — no changes |
| `source/hankweave/standard-operating-procedures.md` | 10-30, 34-36 | Repository structure section — needs update |
| `source/hankweave/.gitignore` | Full | May need additions for docs build artifacts |
| `source/hankweave/scripts/test-sync-local.ts` | 159-175 | Verification list — needs `docs` added |

### Research sources

- [Bun Workspaces](https://bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces) — native workspace support via `package.json` `workspaces` field
- [Bun Catalogs](https://bun.sh/docs/install/catalogs) — optional shared dependency versioning (not needed initially)
- [git subtree merges](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-git/about-git-subtree-merges) — for preserving docs repo history

---

## d. Conventions and Patterns

### Observed code conventions

1. **Scripts are TypeScript** — all build/release/sync scripts are `.ts` files run with `bun`
2. **Relative paths from `import.meta.dir`** — scripts use `path.join(import.meta.dir, "..")` to resolve project root
3. **`Bun.spawn` for shell commands** — scripts use `Bun.spawn(["sh", "-c", cmd])` rather than Node's `child_process`
4. **Two-space indent, 100-char line width** — enforced by Biome
5. **LF line endings** — enforced by `.gitattributes`
6. **No shared state between packages** — docs don't import from runtime; only schema files are copied
7. **Strip lists are explicit** — both `sync-public.ts` and `release.ts` maintain explicit lists of files/dirs to remove

### Patterns to follow

- Add `docs` to existing strip lists rather than creating new mechanisms
- Keep the root `package.json` as the runtime's package.json (add `workspaces` field only)
- Don't introduce Turborepo or other tooling — Bun workspaces is sufficient
- Keep separate `tsconfig.json` per workspace (they have incompatible settings)
- Don't introduce workspace dependencies (`workspace:*`) between docs and runtime — the schema copy is a script-level operation

### Patterns to avoid

- Don't move the runtime into a subdirectory (would break dozens of paths)
- Don't create a shared `tsconfig.base.json` (the two configs are too different)
- Don't add a `bun` workspace filter to CI scripts (just let everything install and run from root)

---

## e. Decision Points and Judgement Calls

### Decision 1: Keep the runtime at the repo root

**Chosen**: The runtime stays at root. The docs site moves into `docs/`.

**Reasoning**: The runtime has 6 scripts, 3 CI workflows, 3 composite actions, build/release/sync pipelines, and extensive relative path usage. Moving it into a subdirectory would require changing every one of these. The docs site has no CI of its own (Vercel builds it), no complex scripts, and one `package.json`. Moving the docs in is a fraction of the work.

**Trade-off**: The root `package.json` serves dual purpose as both workspace root and runtime package. This is a recognized Bun workspace pattern and works correctly — the root package is an "implicit workspace member" by default.

**Impact**: Minimal disruption to existing workflows. The main changes are:
- Adding `"workspaces": ["docs"]` to root `package.json`
- Updating 2-3 file paths in scripts
- Adding `docs` to strip lists

### Decision 2: Flatten the docs repo structure

**Chosen**: Move `hankweave-docs/nextra-site/*` contents directly into `docs/` (not `docs/nextra-site/`).

**Reasoning**: The `nextra-site/` wrapper exists because the docs repo has a root with README, notes, and plan directories. In the monorepo, these don't need a separate layer. The `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `next.config.mjs`, and all source files go directly in `docs/`.

**Alternative considered**: Keeping `docs/nextra-site/` as-is. This preserves the original structure but adds an unnecessary level of nesting. It also means `"workspaces": ["docs/nextra-site"]` which is less clean.

**What to do with `hankweave-docs/` non-nextra files**: The `README.md` at docs repo root, `notes/`, and `plan/` directories are development artifacts. They can either:
- Be discarded (they're internal planning docs)
- Be moved to an `intermediates/` entry documenting the docs site
- Be kept at `docs/` level alongside the nextra files

**Recommendation**: Discard `notes/` and `plan/` (they're historical planning docs). Keep the `README.md` as `docs/README.md` if desired, but it's not required.

### Decision 3: Don't use `workspace:*` dependencies

**Chosen**: No workspace dependency between docs and runtime.

**Reasoning**: The docs site doesn't import from the runtime. The only data flow is schema JSON files copied by `generate-schemas.ts`. This is a script-level file copy, not a package dependency. Adding a `workspace:*` dependency would incorrectly suggest the docs depend on the runtime as a package.

**When to revisit**: If the docs site ever needs to import TypeScript types or utilities from the runtime (e.g., for auto-generated API reference), add `workspace:*` at that point.

### Decision 4: Convert the existing hankweave repo, don't create new

**Chosen**: Modify `SouthBridgeAI/hankweave` in-place to become the monorepo.

**Reasoning**: All CI workflows, GitHub secrets, branch protection rules, Linear integration, and team permissions are already configured on this repo. Creating a new repo would require reconfiguring everything. The existing git history stays intact. The docs files are brought in via a merge commit (or `git subtree add` if history preservation is desired).

**Impact**: No disruption to existing CI/CD. No need to update secrets, protections, or integrations.

### Decision 5: No Turborepo

**Chosen**: Use Bun workspaces alone, no Turborepo.

**Reasoning**: Two packages don't need task orchestration or caching. The runtime builds and tests independently. The docs site builds independently on Vercel. There's no dependency chain requiring `^build` semantics. Adding Turborepo would increase complexity with no clear benefit.

**When to revisit**: If more packages are added (e.g., a shared types package, a CLI package), or if CI times become a problem and caching would help.

### Decision 6: Single lockfile at root

**Chosen**: One `bun.lock` at the repo root, replacing both existing lockfiles.

**Reasoning**: Bun workspaces uses a single root lockfile. Both workspace packages' dependencies are resolved and locked together. This is how Bun workspaces work by default — there's no option for per-workspace lockfiles.

**Impact**: The `bun.lock` from `hankweave` and the `bun.lock` from `hankweave-docs/nextra-site` are both replaced by a regenerated root `bun.lock`. The first `bun install` after migration will generate this.

### Over/under engineering line

- **Under**: Not adding path filtering to CI (docs changes trigger runtime tests). Acceptable for now — CI runs are fast and infrequent enough.
- **Under**: Not using Bun catalogs for shared TypeScript version. Acceptable — the projects only share TypeScript and it's fine to have independent versions.
- **Over**: Adding Turborepo, shared configs, workspace link scripts, or monorepo-specific CI tooling. Not needed for two packages.
- **Right level**: Adding `docs` to strip lists, updating one path in `generate-schemas.ts`, updating the SOP doc. Minimal changes that make the monorepo work.

---

### Existing tests affected

**None of the existing unit, integration, or E2E tests should be affected.** The runtime code is unchanged — no server files, no type files, no config files are modified. Only scripts and metadata files are touched.

2. **E2E init tests** — Test the `--init` scaffolding flow. The runtime code is unchanged so these should pass.
3. **Any test that reads `package.json`** — The only change is adding a `"workspaces"` field, which shouldn't affect anything that reads version, name, or dependencies.

### New tests needed

No new automated tests are strictly required. The migration is a structural change, not a code change. Verification is manual:

1. `bun install` succeeds at root and installs both workspaces
2. `bun run build` still produces correct dist output
3. `bun run generate-schemas` writes to both locations
4. `docs/` build works: `cd docs && bun run build`
5. Sync dry-run strips `docs/` correctly

### Edge cases to consider

1. **npm publish from root** — `npm publish` uses `"files"` field. The `docs/` directory is NOT in the `"files"` array (`["dist", "shims", "schemas"]`), so it won't be included in the npm package. Verify this with `npm pack --dry-run`.

### Bun workspaces

- [bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces](https://bun.sh/docs/install/workspaces) — primary reference
- Root package can be a workspace member itself (important for our "runtime at root" approach)
- `bun install` at root installs all workspace dependencies
- `bun --filter <name> <script>` runs scripts in specific workspaces (useful for `bun --filter hankweave-docs build`)

### Vercel monorepo support

- Vercel's Root Directory setting specifies which subdirectory contains the deployable project
- "Ignored Build Step" can filter deploys to only docs changes
